quest.title: The Narzissenkreuz Adventure
quest.description: In Fontaine, where there aren't supposed to be any Oceanids, you meet a tiny Oceanid...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.num: Ann of the Narzissenkreuz: Act I
chapter.title: The Narzissenkreuz Adventure

dialogues.text: Ah! You there! You look most reliable, good knight. Please, help us!

choices.text: We certainly do look reliable enough...

response.text: The evil minions of the fell dragon Narcissus have surrounded Petit Chou! We must help her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Petit Chou"...?

choices.text: "Narcissus"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, never mind these weird names. This seems serious! Let's get over there and lend a hand!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Thank you! My name is Ann, a member of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team. Please, come with me!

choices.text: Yeah, forget the names. Just lead the way.
What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess we won't be worrying about this mysterious bubble cannon anymore.
Well done, soldiers! Assemble!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, where's that voice coming from? Does "soldiers" refer to us?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Wonderful! It seems that Colonel Kate is still here. Let's go meet up with him.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Eek! Get away from me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that... the "Petit Chou" you were referring to, Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That's right! Please, help her!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where's the rest of your team?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aren't you the same as the Orchestre Jak?

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: What? We're as different as night and day! Why, that Jak... One day, people like him will warp the very essence of our resistance movement!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Isn't the Orchestre Jak's goal to defeat Narcissus and save Princess Lyris— sorry, Ms. Lyris? Aren't your goals the same?

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Aye, and there's the rub! He does not recognize her as our rightful Princess! He is, simply put, a problem waiting to happen!

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Today, he refuses to recognize her! What will he do tomorrow? Lead his Orchestre to overturn the kingdom!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Uh, {NICKNAME}, what do we do? Jak does seem like the sorta guy who might do that!)

choices.text: (That's an internal issue.)

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Alright, alright. Our goals are aligned! We're all doing this for Princess Lyris and the Reconquista, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. It seems like the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom's situation is kinda complicated... Wait. What about your team?

choices.text: (Let's put a pin in that first.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That did happen...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: R—Really? You're so strong...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #It is our great fortune to have met you, good knight {NICKNAME}. It seems that the time has come at last for the Reconquista! The Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team shall reclaim the realm and rescue Princess Lyris.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Come, Petit Chou, let us do as we planned. First, let's get rid of all this foul water!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: I... I'll do my best!

dialogues.speaker: Ann & Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Alrighty!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh! Paimon's starting to get confused about what counts as a dragon...

choices.text: I'm confused as well...

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Our purpose defines our essence. At this time, we are the heroes challenging the wicked dragon, and he is the wicked dragon. This is sufficient.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: Huh, this must be what Al means when he says "A rose by any other name would smell just as sweet!"

response.speaker: Al
response.text: That is precisely the case, dear Petit Chou. Were you not called "Petit Chou," you would still be my dearest younger sister.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So, so long as that's the tower your Princess sleeps in, the one lurking atop the tower is the fell dragon Narcissus. Is that right?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: No, I fear. As we stated previously, he is "not here now," which is why we were able to win our way here so easily. That up there is the dragon's hatred made manifest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's so complicated... Can't it just be an ordinary statue?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like, you know, Narcissus commanding his underlings to make an image of him on the highest tower, so as to show off his greatness, and force all the people of the land to look upon him... or something?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Well... You actually make a reasonable point, Paimon. But if that was the case, then we should still have been able to see it even before Petit Chou made the foul water disappear, right?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But instead, Narcissus's evil has melded with the waters, which is why his wicked intent crystallized into that image once the waters were drained.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that seriously how it happened...?

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: The fell dragon is truly terrifying. My talons hurt just looking at him...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Well, we have our knight, {NICKNAME}, so we should be fine even if he is present, yes?

choices.text: It'd be best if he wasn't home all the same...

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Humility becomes a knight indeed.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Let us move on, then. With you by our side, we have nothing to fear!

choices.text: It's just a lil' dragon.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: #Hehe, that's our {NICKNAME} for you!

choices.text: I never understood that in the first place.
Categories are just a social construct. There is no objective meaning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Come on, that can't be right! How would we be able to communicate and understand this world otherwise?

response.speaker: Al
response.text: I agree with the knight here. Our categories should not define our essence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, all this water... Is this some kind of Oceanid magic?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Phew. The defensive power has weakened. There will also be less obstacles for us to fight from here on out.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Phew... This is so tiring...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: #Ann, {NICKNAME}, let's go help my brother Al!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your brother? Is he another character?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Well, Petit Chou and I can't be the only members of the team. We don't quite think *that* highly of ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: We certainly aren't as strong as you or Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Al covered our escape when we retreated. Now that Narcissus's power is waning, let's go help him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, then let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: We charged bravely into the Bubble Formation!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, and where's your team?

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: We charged bravely into the Bubble Formation! And as for the rest... please, don't ask...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Colonel Kate's got problems, too...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Well, he is up against immense firepower... or should I say, waterpower.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: What's next for you?

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: I plan on going behind enemy lines to see what can be done there. After all, it should be quite easy to go up there now that the Bubble Formation has been broken. I mean, I can't lose to some new recruit, can I?

choices.text: There's no shame in losing to me...

response.speaker: Colonel Kate
response.text: Hmph! Regardless, I shall return when the sun sinks into the sea, victory in hand! Let us meet again before the high tower.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Colonel Kate bounces away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. There's neither sun nor sea here!

choices.text: This isn't a competition...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like Mondstadt's Dvalin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Dvalin's a whole different story from Oceanids. Dvalin's super blue, his wings are huge, and he can fly...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: What!? That's... exactly like the fell dragon!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like Liyue's Azhdaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who... became the embodiment of primal energies and Liyue's enemy?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I see. So it was a being as evil as Narcissus, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, not at all!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: And how are they different? Narcissus represents primordial regression and aggregation, and is our foe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... Uh... But Azhdaha's from Liyue! That's a huge difference... right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like Sumeru's Apep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A being whose true form cannot be grasped by humanity, and who can summon all manner of servants...

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: That does sound quite like Narcissus. Inscrutable and a master of many servants. That must've been a grueling battle. Very impressive!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no, we've definitely met other dragons before...

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: The name is merely an analogy, for we weave resistance like an orchestra in our struggle against Narcissus as we seek to rescue Ms. Lyris.

choices.text: Don't you mean "Princess Lyris"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Isn't Lyris a Princess?

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Well, both terms refer to the same person. But leaving that aside, we should...

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Listen well. The title "Princess" is a rigid, hierarchical term of address, a product of an oppressive system. It was a title whose merit is birth, not labor or wisdom.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: *sigh* Here we go again...

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: If the universe was a more rational one, there would be no gods, no kings, and certainly no princes or princesses. Nor would there be mystical powers that only a few may wield.

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Do you follow me thus far?

choices.text: There will always be those who desire special privileges.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It is a deplorable state of affairs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... This sounds really deep, but it's also confusing Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But not doing anything all day while being able to enjoy delicious Sweet Madames is pretty nice. Is there anything wrong with that?

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: See! If there are some who will reap the benefits despite doing no labor, then there must be some who shall have to do more to compensate.

choices.text: Like me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Um, uh... Thanks a lot, {NICKNAME}... and sorry? Paimon promises that she'll eat less in the future. Honest!

response.speaker: Al
response.text: This has been a very interesting conversation, but please allow me to interject. Dear Jak, good knight, may we now begin discussing our next course of action in our rescue of Princess Lyris...

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: #Hmph! Silencing voices you do not want to hear, I see! Oh, {NICKNAME}! Come, see the repression inherent in the system! Help! Help! Al's repressing me!

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Jak, you...!

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: Al isn't doing that! He's a good person, he wouldn't bully you!

response.speaker: Al
response.text: *sigh* Dear sister, please, do not lose your temper over this.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: If you have more to say, Jak, why don't we find a corner and settle this like gentlemen? Hmm?

choices.text: Can I trouble you all to stop for a second...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Please, everyone. Aren't we comrades? We've all gathered to rescue Princess... or "Ms." Lyris, after all!

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Hmph. We count as such, I suppose. We shall cooperate... even though my final goal is to create a more beautiful world for Ms. Lyris.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Let us shake hands then. Comrades?

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: You have wings, I have webbed feet. If you think these apt replacements for hands, then we shall do so, comrade.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Jak and Al shake hands... awkwardly.\nIf nothing else, they extend their wing and webbed foot, and tap them together.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: Please get along with him, Al.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Of course, dear sister, do not worry. We are united in one cause.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Alright, alright, now that the problem is solved...

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Pah. "Problem"? This is but the manifestation of a deeper issue...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Jak, please!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so... What do we do next, Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Hmm? Oh. Right! I almost forgot that we were here to save the Princess. Why, I was starting to think that I'd brought such capable help along, just to let them listen to two boys squabble!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: As for the situation... Ask Al and Jak to explain. I... need a moment to cool off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ann's having a tough time too, huh...

choices.text: I've heard enough. See you around.
Stop squabbling. We all have the same goal.
Paimon lacks the strength for labor. Thus, such compensation is my obligation.

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: ...It would indeed seem so. Your line of thinking is fair and responsible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Um... Then, thanks a lot, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! Paimon does do work in her own way, doesn't she?

choices.text: It doesn't matter to me. Paimon's happiness is mine as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon hopes you can be happy, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait a minute. In that case, wouldn't {NICKNAME} be happy if {M#he}{F#she} makes Paimon happy...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that means making Paimon happy more is good for you too! That's how this works, right?

choices.text: ...Didn't you put your name on your organization as well?

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: An orchestra must have a conductor, lest no music be made out of cacophony.

choices.text: This rabbit hole's not for me...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We must destroy the three <color=#00E1FFFF>Bubble Formations</color> set up by Narcissus before we head up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are those exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: They are underhanded contraptions powered by <color=#00E1FFFF>Hydrograna</color> that can bombard intruders from a great distance... Perhaps you might have already seen one on the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: Ann speaks true. The road ahead will be vastly more perilous if we do not first destroy those Formations.

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: Hmph. Kate should have been in charge of eliminating them before we attacked. But it seems that he might have been smashed into seafoam already.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Don't say that! We should be hoping that he made it — he is our comrade in the end, isn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: In that case, our next task is the destruction of the Bubble Formations! After that, let's go to the small fountain and see what we find there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #In that case, leave it to {NICKNAME}. From what Petit Chou and Al have said, it seems like only {M#his}{F#her} attacks will work...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Ohh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon didn't mean to put you down! You guys have been fighting Narcissus and trying to save Princess Lyris for so long... But just leave this bit to {NICKNAME}, alright?

choices.text: That's right. Leave it to me.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: You have my thanks.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Alright! In that case, let me lead the way!

choices.text: You may see it as a knight doing their duty.
I'd like to see where this "story" goes, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An... Orchestre?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that some kind of musical troupe?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds oddly similar to Kate's Resistance Front.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's what Paimon wanted to say too!

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: Kate's Resistance Front? Bah! That disorganized, untrained militia are but rabble!

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: We here at Orchestre Jak are a collective of people from all walks of life who carry out operations based on our personal abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon knows! The Orchestre's in charge of music and the Resistance Front resists, so they're not the same at heart, like bards and knights!

choices.text: You're pretty difficult yourself.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: He wasn't always like this. He once had a really good heart, and loved to cry. He would take care of the younger children...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But one day, he said that he would never cry again, and later still, he changed. This might be due to Rene, I fear... and Rene changed too...

choices.text: And who's Rene?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Um, sorry, where was I? Right, our course of action. You should ask Jak and the others. He and Al might argue a lot, but they're actually good friends.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Alain split with them. But as for me...

choices.text: See you.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: You should ask Jak and the others about our course of action. He and Al might argue a lot, but they're actually good friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jak! You...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Paimon! Don't...

choices.text: (Knock it off, or we're going to start this all over again.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hmph, Paimon knows!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *cough* Ann told us that you could explain the situation...

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Allow me to speak first then, honored Knight and Paimon. Concerning the tower before us, Narcissus has been unable to overcome it. As such, the Princess is still safe.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: At that time, when all seemed lost, the Princess gave her greatest treasure to us, and that was the "time" that belonged to her.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: After she lost that time, the Princess and the tower she dwells in both fell into a stagnant, dreamless slumber. In remembrance of her, we named our fallen realm the Annapausis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what does that mean...?

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Because it has completely stagnated, Narcissus has also been unable to taint anything within... That's more or less our situation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean "more or less our situation"? Firstly, how would someone give anyone else their "time"?

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: But it's true! Princess Lyris did share her time with us. Narcissus would constantly plot to invade, but with the time she gave us, we became far stronger!

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: For example... My brother, Al, can usually only defeat one foe at once, but with more "time," he can vanquish four or even five at one go!

response.speaker: Al
response.text: A most vivid example. Thank you for your explanation, dear Petit Chou.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: #Hehe. Well, I hope you understand now, {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

choices.text: Not at all, in fact.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. How do you even give your time to other people!?

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Do these details matter? Is this not similar to how feudal nobles would hire sharecroppers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Share... croppers? How do those things even connect!? Are you trying to say that exchanging time for pay is a form of giving your time to others?

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Only a very small part of the wealth a sharecropper creates will belong to him. If this is understood and regarded as normal by all, then what is there about this situation that is hard to comprehend?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Ugh, he got Paimon!)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Why are you debating with an Oceanid?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (There's too much oddity at play here. Let's just leave this aside for now.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true... Alright, uh, Paimon totally gets it!

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Narcissus has spent long years since searching for the Princess's treasure. Only its power can cause time in the tower to flow again, and only then will its locked gates open.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Thus he summoned waters brimming with wicked intent to drown the kingdom, and created underlings unnumbered and many magical devices besides.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: All this was done to hunt us Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team members down and seize the treasure that should have been in our hands.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. "Should have"?

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: Before, we had another older brother... Ney. In those terrifying days, he took the treasure and fled alongside us, but he dissolved into the waters while covering us.

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: I miss him so much.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: We were very good friends.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: I hate the dragon, even though I know that these feelings are not good. But I miss Ney. He was like my real brother, just like Al.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, we're... sorry for your loss...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if that's the case, how are we supposed to save Princess Lyris? The treasure has sealed the tower, and it can only be opened again with said treasure...

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Well. When they, ah... How do I put this? While they were "consolidating our rear lines," we of Orchestre Jak obtained some key intelligence that has allowed us to ascertain the treasure's location.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: Really? You have?

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Of course. It is right over there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? In the sky? As in, in the water in the sky?

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Before Ney dissolved, he used the last of his strength to purify a patch of water in the firmament. It was there that he hid the treasure.

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: What an irony. It seems that Narcissus has gotten too used to looking down upon the citizenry below, and has not been in the habit of looking up — and there, the treasure has been hidden all along.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: I see. Well, it does sound like something Ney would come up with.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How do we get up there, though?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Could Petit Chou and Al take us up there?

response.speaker: Al
response.text: A very imaginative idea... but unfortunately, impractical.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: If we go up there, we should find a small fountain full of magic. Options may open to us should we reach it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you feeling better now, Ann...?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Thank you, Paimon, but you need not worry.

choices.text: Yes, yes, I understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (What did you even understand!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (There's too much oddity at play here. Let's just leave this aside for now.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Alright then, Paimon totally gets it too!

choices.text: She gave you her what now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Time," you say...

choices.text: Is there anything I need to do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello!

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: *sniffs*

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Mori, no!

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: Woof, woof! Bad people!

talks.objective: Use force to clear up any misunderstandings!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We must destroy the three <color=#00E1FFFF>Bubble Formations</color> set up by Narcissus before we head up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are those exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: They are underhanded contraptions powered by Hydrograna that can bombard intruders from a great distance... Perhaps you might have already seen one on the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's what you call those annoying bubble cannons!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That's right. We already solved one part of the problem on the way here, but we'll need to finish the job if our road up is to be made safe.

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: Hmph. Kate should have been in charge of eliminating them before we attacked. But it seems that he might have been smashed into seafoam already.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Don't say that! We should be hoping that he made it — he is our comrade in the end, isn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, our next task is the destruction of the remaining Bubble Formations! After that, let's go to the small fountain and see what we find there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #In that case, leave it to {NICKNAME}. From what Petit Chou and Al have said, it seems like only {M#his}{F#her} attacks will work...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Ohh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon didn't mean to put you down! You guys have been fighting Narcissus and trying to save Princess Lyris for so long... But just leave this bit to {NICKNAME}, alright?

choices.text: That's right. Leave it to me.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: You have my thanks.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Alright! In that case, let me lead the way!

choices.text: You may see it as a knight doing their duty.
I'd like to see where this "story" goes, too.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Silly dog, Mori! Bad! They're good people!

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: Woof, understood. Give paw?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You really are a dog...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon shake hands with Mori.\nIt's a slippery experience, as one might expect of a "dog" made of water.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Great, now we're all introduced. Don't attack them, okay, Mori?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're a dog. This makes much more sense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does it? Does it really? How does Mori resemble a dog at all?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Didn't Al say that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Don't you go believing that "purpose defines essence" nonsense... and even if you do, Paimon won't!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But that's what Mori is, though. A silly dog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, whatever! If an Oceanid can be an evil dragon, then a Forest Boar can be a dog! Alright? Alright!

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: I am a silly dog, yes. Woof.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: And you've been a good boy, haven't you, guarding this place?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, is Mori a member of your team?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No... I mean, Mori is a dog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But a duck, a frog, a finch, and a squirrel can join... So why can't a dog?

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: Mori is Mori. Must protect the princess.

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: A long, long time ago, Mori played here. With the Princess, Al, Petit Chou, Ney, and Jak.

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: But the air and water were later filled with the scent of evil, and everyone left.

dialogues.speaker: Mori
dialogues.text: Only the Princess remains. So I protect her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's Princess Lyris...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! It was mentioned earlier that the Princess lost her treasure, which is why everything stagnated. So this is where it was!

choices.text: Problem solved!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: This is just a statue of the Princess. She's still in the tower.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously? Another "looks like it, but not really"?

response.speaker: Mori
response.text: Woof, woof? Not the Princess?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Nope. Princess Lyris is in her tower.

response.speaker: Mori
response.text: There are two Princesses?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: No, silly. This one's not real.

response.speaker: Mori
response.text: Woof, woof? Not the Princess?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Well, try giving it a sniff.

response.speaker: Mori
response.text: *sniffs*

response.speaker: Mori
response.text: Woof, woof? Not the Princess?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Told you so.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it's an understandable mistake. In this Annapausis, a boar is a dog, an Oceanid is an evil dragon, and the evil dragon turned out to be a statue...

choices.text: And a duck and a finch are siblings...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly. Ugh, Paimon can feel her sense of what's real or not slipping away the longer we stay here...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: *cough* Well, um, let's not sweat the small stuff, alright?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Okay, Mori. Be a good doggie and descend the tower, then meet up with everyone.

response.speaker: Mori
response.text: Okay. What about you, Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Me? Well, I'm going up with {NICKNAME} and Paimon to reclaim the Princess's treasure.

response.speaker: Mori
response.text: I see. Okay. Bye-bye.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then. What do we do now?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Use these bubbles. The Princess would make these back when she would play with us, and they would fly very high up indeed. We would fly around in those bubbles, touring the realm.

choices.text: That sounds quite exciting...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whatever the case, we just need to sit in the bubble, and it'll take us up there, right?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: That's right! In the meantime, I'll do my best to control the bubbles' direction.

choices.text: That sounds like the trick those Hydro Abyss Mages pull...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Hey! Don't say that about the Princess's magic!

choices.text: And a squirrel is a Colonel...
Isn't the princess in the tower, though?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: That's right. This is only a statue of her.

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: But before we ascend, we need to deal with the various Bubble Formations to make safe our path.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bubble Formations... There's three of them, right? If that's the case, we've already taken them all out!

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: My, that's our mighty knight and Paimon for you! Ah, it's just a shame that I was unable to watch the battle between you and the Three Royal Blades of Narcissus in person!

choices.text: They were super weak...

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Ah, what reliable allies you are. When you've the time, please do tell Petit Chou and I of that valorous deed!

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: Please do!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: In that case, to the fountain! We'll find a way to access the waters above and retrieve Princess Lyris's treasure!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Al, Petit Chou, Jak, this place is yours to guard!

choices.text: It was a grinding battle, but we ultimately emerged triumphant.
...Sorry, the what of the what now?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #The three leaders who were defending the three Bubble Formations. They were quickly dispatched by {NICKNAME}, though, as if they were mere chaff.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: More than once, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Ah... I'm saved...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait. So Petit Chou is a Finch...?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Petit Chou is Petit Chou.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Regardless, it's good that you're well, Petit Chou! Now let me introduce these two...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Um, actually, I haven't yet asked you two your names...

choices.text: I'm "a knight who looks most reliable."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Are you seriously still hung up about that? {M#He}{F#She}'s {NICKNAME}, and Paimon's Paimon!

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: #Thank you, Knight {NICKNAME}, Squire Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Squire...?

choices.text: Squire Paimon, attend to my weapons.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Gah, you've got it all wrong! Paimon's no squire. She's {NICKNAME}'s companion. Actually, wait a moment... Your weapons need maintaining?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Indeed, there's been a misunderstanding. We're companions, of course.

choices.text: ...And don't you get that twisted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah! That's more like it.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: I see, I see. My apologies, Paimon! I am Petit Chou, a member of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team. If not for your help, I might have...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Well, Narcissus has girded his subordinates with the Aegis of Four Orthants, so our powers are unable to overcome them. That's how it is.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But with you and your companion on our side, good knight, we shall have nothing to fear!

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: The Princess will be pleased!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uh, one moment! Who's this Princess again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, what is this Adventure Team of yours? And what's going on with this Narcissus?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Well... This is how things went. A long, long time ago, this was a kingdom of unparalleled gladness. The children and Princess Lyris lived happily together here.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But later, the kingdom fell to the predations of Narcissus, a fell dragon who had designs on the Princess and her treasures.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Princess Lyris hid herself away in a high tower and entered a deep slumber. That is why we now name the kingdom "Annapausis."

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Narcissus filled Annapausis with bitter waters. That which we just defeated was an evil being born from those waters, an entity that opposes the Reconquista.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: This time, we attempted to infiltrate this place and rescue the Princess while the dragon was absent. However, we ran into a great many foes, and ultimately, we failed.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #But now that we have you and Paimon on our side, {NICKNAME}, we have nothing to fear!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Moreover, we have a Princess, a kingdom, and a wicked dragon... Tradition and the stories dictate that we must also have a knight — yes, a mighty and righteous knight like you, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Stories?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon's not sure what you're going on about, but if it's dragons you want, {NICKNAME}'s beaten 'em before.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Really? You have?

choices.text: Tradition?
Well, I have defeated a dragon in the past.
...Although I have indeed considered getting a squire in the past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you really want one? Seems like this journey has been pretty tough for you, huh...

choices.text: Squire Paimon, my shoulders ache.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Gah, you've got it all wrong! Paimon's no squire. She's {NICKNAME}'s companion!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Indeed, there's been a misunderstanding. We're companions, of course.

choices.text: ...And don't you get that twisted.
...Although I have indeed considered getting a squire in the past.
She's not my squire, we're companions.
#{NICKNAME}'s the name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon's Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Al! You're safe! I was so worried...

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: Ah, my dear Petit Chou — and you too, Ann! We meet again at last. In those darkest of days, I thought of you, and drew strength to fight on from those thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: Thank you, noble warriors, you who have come forth to uphold the cause of justice. Why, had I arms as slender as yours, I would tip my hat to honor you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's no need to be so prim and proper...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ann introduces you and Paimon to Al and explains what happened previously.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, but why's a finch's older brother a duck?

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: Why a "duck," you ask? Are such definitions important? I have a supple body, an iron will, and webbed feet with which to tread water. Of these I am proud, and that is enough.

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: And Petit Chou is Petit Chou. The sphere is the shape closest to perfection, and the most complicated of all shapes. I am most proud of my sister.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: S—Seriously, brother, what are you talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Actually, {NICKNAME}, what *is* Al talking about?)

choices.text: (He means that we shouldn't dwell too much on these details.)

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: We members of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team are disparate indeed, but we have one goal. We shall save Princess Lyris, and we shall defeat the fell dragon Narcissus!

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Well said. The person I am now knows only that the one who stands before me is a noble and valiant knight who possesses the iron will needed to defeat Narcissus. That is enough for me.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: Usually, the mightier the will, the larger the form needed to be its vessel, as it is in the case of Narcissus. This knight's stature is much like mine, and yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Seriously, the first and last thing Paimon understood here was "Narcissus." You're always going on about Narcissus this and Narcissus that... But what is it, really?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Look up, above Princess Lyris's tower — that is Narcissus.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? That wasn't there before the water rose...

choices.text: ...Isn't that just an Oceanid?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But that is the fell dragon Narcissus.

response.speaker: Al
response.text: The dragon who invaded the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: And its wings are very huge and frightening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...But it's an Oceanid, isn't it?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, you have seen much. What, then, should a dragon look like?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you're talking about the dragons we've fought before, they'd be...

choices.text: Good golly gosh, the fell dragon Narcissus!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waaaait a minute, that's an Oceanid no matter how you look at it, not a dragon!

choices.text: (I don't know... but it's probably not important.)

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Jak...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Thank goodness you're safe!

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: Hmm. As I thought, you were the ones who emptied the water out. Excellent, excellent! If I had hands like yours, yellow and white ones, I would be applauding already.

dialogues.speaker: Al
dialogues.text: Dear friend, please show some respect. Petit Chou is doing her best...

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: Hmph. You are right, I suppose. She has done nothing wrong. Ultimately...

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: Forget it. The yellow and white ones here... Who are they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yellow and white... You mean us?

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: And who else would I mean? Does Petit Chou look yellower to you? Or does Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! You... you blue frog!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Alright, alright, Paimon, please don't be angry. Jak, this is knight {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Jak
dialogues.text: Hmph. A knight, you say... Then I suppose this Paimon is the squire?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no! Come on, why does everyone call Paimon that!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon is no squire.

choices.text: Paimon is a bard whose task is to record my adventures.

response.speaker: Petit Chou
response.text: Is that how it is? No wonder Paimon's such a good talker!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! You stop that, {NICKNAME}, or Paimon's gonna come up with a... lively limerick to give you a licking the likes of which you've never seen!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, we're companions, alright? Companions!

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: I see. Then you are not some minor feudal warrior. Not in the usual sense, anyway. Are you, then, some "honorary knight," one with a title that comes with little benefit?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME} is an Honorary Knight, but {M#he}{F#she} got it in Mondstadt for heroically doing battle with Stormterror!

response.speaker: Jak
response.text: Ah, then you are a dutiful, capable warrior. Very good! In that case, welcome to Orchestre Jak.

choices.text: Paimon's my companion.

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Ann! You look well. That is good. These two are reinforcements, then?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yes! They are...

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Halt. I do not wish to know soldiers' names.

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Amidst cruel battle, anyone can be turned into ruptured bubbles and scattered foam at any time. Knowing the names of the troops will only cast a shadow upon our final victory.

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: I just need to know one thing. Are they the reinforcements you sought?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yes, but...

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Very good. Fresh hands will help us continue our suppression of the two remaining Bubble Formations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: About that Bubble Formation...

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Next time, soldier, you will give your report first before asking questions. Yes, the Formations are places of unparalleled peril — not to mention the three mighty subordinates that Narcissus has placed within them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, about that... We've actually cleared all the Formations...

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: What!? Why didn't you say so earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We've been trying to tell you, but you haven't been listening!

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: Um... Ha. Hahaha. Well then, it's good to see that everyone is well! So, Ann, who are these people again?

choices.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}, and this is Paimon.

response.speaker: Colonel Kate
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, hmm? Pleased to make your acquaintance.

response.speaker: Colonel Kate
response.text: It's a pleasure to have new blood like you in Kate's Resistance Front. Let us fight for Princess Lyris and the Reconquista!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kate's Resistance Front, huh. Are you guys the same thing as the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Let me think... "We are now the same thing," is how I would put it.

response.speaker: Colonel Kate
response.text: Indeed. We have the same objective and plan of action. It is only because I have more combat experience that I am a colonel with my own force.

choices.text: #{NICKNAME}, reporting in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon, reporting in!

response.speaker: Colonel Kate
response.text: #Very good, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! Very good!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Since the Bubble Formations are gone, let's head to the little fountain. It's just over there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't know much about music.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wonderful. I'm a master musician.

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: We charged bravely into the Bubble Formation!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, and where's your team?

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: We charged bravely into the Bubble Formation! And as for the rest... please, don't ask...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Colonel Kate's got problems, too...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Well, he is up against immense firepower... or should I say, waterpower.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: What's next for you?

dialogues.speaker: Colonel Kate
dialogues.text: I plan on going behind enemy lines to see what can be done there. After all, it should be quite easy to go up there now that the Bubble Formation has been broken. I mean, I can't lose to some new recruit, can I?

choices.text: There's no shame in losing to me...

response.speaker: Colonel Kate
response.text: Hmph! Regardless, I shall return when the sun sinks into the sea, victory in hand! Let us meet again before the high tower.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Colonel Kate bounces away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. There's neither sun nor sea here!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Since the Bubble Formations are gone, let's head to the little fountain. It's just over there!

choices.text: This isn't a competition...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Hmm? Well, after the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom was conquered by Narcissus the fell dragon...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We banded together to rescue Princess Lyris and reclaim the realm. That's the basic answer, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound basic at all, but we'll talk about that later. We've got people to save first!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That's right. Come with me, this way!

dialogues.speaker: Evil Fang of Narcissus
dialogues.text: Mwa—hahahah! I have you now, Petit Chou of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: I—If you don't leave, I'm gonna get serious! Grrr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This reminds Paimon of the time you became a knight, {NICKNAME}. After fighting the dragon, we were sent off to the temples of the Four Winds...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Ooh! To beseech their aid?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Why was that, again? Paimon recalls that we destroyed something inside the temples to decrease the dragon's power...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I see, so they were temples in name, but dens of evil in truth!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: Um, were there four temples of the Four Winds, or just one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There were three, actually... Huh, why *were* there only three?

dialogues.speaker: Petit Chou
dialogues.text: That's right. Why three?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been quite a while... There must've been a reason. Paimon just doesn't remember it...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Hmm. That does make sense. The trivial details of a brilliant knight's deeds wouldn't matter much, would they?
